text:
Tyler Bertuzzi scored 32 goals last season and Evolving-Hockey rated him worth 2.8 wins above replacement, 20th among 401 forwards, despite teammates in the bottom 1% by their measure. This season he has 3 goals and 7 points in 20 games, and Bleacher Nation's headline put it plainly: "The Blackhawks Need More From Tyler Bertuzzi."

The decline is in the chances, not just the finish. He is generating 0.66 expected goals per 60 minutes, a measure of the quality of the shots he takes, down from 1.25 last season. His shooting, 13.6%, is normal. He has 2 points in his last ten games.

There is some bad luck around him. Chicago has scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and our numbers flag that as likely to swing back. The bigger concern is at 5-on-5, where the Blackhawks have taken just 40.6% of expected goals with him out there. He has been skating on the top line with Connor Bedard, so the chances should be there to take. What we'd watch is his shot rate: the goals follow it, and right now it isn't there.
headline: Bertuzzi's goals have gone missing in Chicago
